report.executive_thesis:
DIRECT INQUIRY RESOLUTION:
The 5-year compounding outlook for a ₹500,000 allocation split between TCS and Infosys suggests a moderate wealth accumulation trajectory. Based on the optimized SLSQP weights, your capital is projected to grow to a gross terminal value of approximately ₹613,400. This represents a 4.17% CAGR over the 5-year horizon. While these entities remain pillars of the Indian IT sector, the current valuation environment and volatility diffusion suggest that capital appreciation will be sensitive to margin expansion and global discretionary spending cycles.

PORTFOLIO CONVICTION & POSTURE:
The ACCUMULATE_STAGGERED posture with a 75/100 conviction score reflects the necessity of mitigating entry-point risk. Given the current volatility profile, a lump-sum deployment is discouraged. The strategy mandates a systematic entry to capture cost-averaging benefits, particularly as the sector navigates a transition from legacy maintenance to AI-led service integration. For fresh capital of ₹500,000, the focus is on building the position over a 6-month window to neutralize short-term price swings.

QUANTITATIVE VOLATILITY & DOWNSIDE VAR:
The portfolio carries a 1-year 95% Parametric VaR of -29.5% and a Conditional VaR of -38.6%, indicating significant tail-risk exposure during market stress. The 5-year bearish floor (P10) at ₹753.15 highlights a critical quantitative reality: in a prolonged severe downcycle, the combination of high volatility diffusion and sector-specific cyclical stagnation can effectively neutralize the expected drift. While the P50 median projection of ₹1,415.85 suggests a positive outcome, the P10 scenario serves as a reminder that high-beta equity baskets are susceptible to multi-year periods where compounding is offset by valuation compression.

STRUCTURAL CATALYSTS & VALUATION:
The investment thesis rests on the robust operating cash flows and high return on equity (ROE) characteristic of both TCS and Infosys. Key drivers include the acceleration of cloud migration, cybersecurity demand, and the long-term integration of generative AI into enterprise workflows. However, the current valuation multiples necessitate a disciplined approach, as the expected returns are contingent upon these firms maintaining their premium pricing power amidst a competitive global landscape.

STATUTORY TAX DRAG & NET IN-HAND WEALTH:
Under the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, your terminal wealth is subject to a 12.5% LTCG tax on gains exceeding the ₹1.25 Lakh threshold, alongside a 0.1% delivery STT. After accounting for these statutory obligations, the gross final wealth of ₹613,400.05 results in a net post-tax CAGR of 4.13%. This net figure is the primary metric for evaluating the success of your wealth compounding objective against inflation.

PERSONALIZED ACTION BLUEPRINT:
To deploy your ₹500,000 fresh capital effectively, adhere to the following execution plan:
• Allocate ₹301,000 to TCS.NS and ₹199,000 to INFY.NS to maintain the optimal SLSQP weights.
• Implement a 6-month Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) or staggered buy orders. Divide the total capital into 6 equal tranches of approximately ₹83,333.
• Execute one tranche at the start of each month, regardless of market fluctuations, to ensure the portfolio is not fully exposed to a single entry-point valuation.
• Rebalance the portfolio semi-annually to ensure the 60.2/39.8 weight distribution remains intact, preventing drift caused by the relative performance variance between the two stocks.
• Monitor the 4.13% net CAGR target against prevailing inflation rates; if the probability of beating inflation (currently 45.2%) shifts downward due to sustained macro headwinds, consider a tactical review of the allocation.

PERSONALIZED PORTFOLIO GUIDANCE:
For 10-year wealth compounding, your ₹500,000 investment is modeled to compound into ₹613,400 (Base P50 target). Maintain full conviction hold. Rebalance only if asset drifts beyond ±5% of your strategic asset allocation.

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>
